stem: Why does the passage recommend choosing tree species suited to local conditions?
options: Different species always require identical amounts of water.
Local species grow without receiving any care.
Trees from elsewhere cannot provide useful shade.
Unsuitable trees may need repeated replacement.

verdicts.working: The passage says unsuitable trees may fail to thrive and require frequent replacement, matching (A).

working: The passage explains that a tree unable to thrive may need frequent replacement, wasting money and effort; selecting species suited to local soil and rainfall helps avoid this.
solution: Trees unsuited to local soil and rainfall may fail to thrive and require frequent replacement, wasting money and effort. Thus, choosing locally suitable species helps avoid repeated replacement.
